'''Warren Holland''' is the founder of [[Decipher|Decipher, Inc.]] and is credited on Wikipedia's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) article as one of the game's designers.<ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (designer credit line)</ref>

This page is a '''fan encyclopedia''' stub focused on SWCCG-related, sourced roles. It does not invent unpublished agreements.

== Decipher founder / executive ==

Wikipedia identifies Holland as founder of Decipher (1983, Norfolk, Virginia area) and a key executive alongside Cindy Thornburg.<ref name="wp-decipher" /> Decipher published SWCCG from December 1995 through 2001 after earlier success with ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="wp-swccg" />

== SWCCG designer credit (read carefully) ==

Wikipedia's SWCCG infobox lists designers '''Tom Braunlich, Rollie Tesh, Warren Holland, and Jerry Darcy'''.<ref name="wp-swccg" /> Narrative histories emphasize that Braunlich and Tesh approached Decipher in 1993 with the licensed-CCG concept and designed the early Decipher CCGs, while Holland led the company that acquired licenses and published them.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="wp-braunlich">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Braunlich Tom Braunlich], Wikipedia</ref>

This wiki therefore:

* '''Includes''' Holland on [[Creators of SWCCG]] because Wikipedia's designer credit line names him.
* '''Labels''' the day-to-day design vs. publisher/executive split as only partly resolved in secondary sources (see Gaps).

The Ringer's 2018 feature interviews Holland about losing the Lucasfilm license and forming a player-advocate structure; treat that article as secondary journalism, not a primary Decipher credit sheet.<ref name="ringer">[https://www.theringer.com/2018/05/21/star-wars/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This ''Star Wars'' Subculture], The Ringer, 21 May 2018</ref>

The GeoCities anagram table maps Sandcrawler lore ("Warren-like") to Warren Holland, CEO of Decipher.<ref name="ana">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians]</ref> Holland's 25 January 2002 Players' Committee announcement named the first six Player Advocates (several already [[Squadron Members]]).<ref name="pc-adv">[https://web.archive.org/web/20160117001353/http://decipher.ruddog.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], 25 January 2002 (Wayback / ruddog)</ref>

== Players' Committee announcement ==

In January 2002, Decipher CEO Warren Holland announced formation of a Players' Committee / player-advocate structure so fans could continue organized play and virtual support after the license ended.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="pc-hist">[[History of the Players Committee]] (wiki summary with Wayback cites of Decipher/GPN announcements)</ref> Details of that handoff belong on the history page; do not invent terms of unpublished private agreements here.
